summary: Wasatch National Forest rooftop lookout on Salt Lake City's Walker Bank Building, 1939 to about 1948; the building still stands as Walker Center.

facts.design: Three-legged map (alidade) table with a sighting device, no enclosure, set beneath a three-story steel advertising tower on the roof
facts.agency: Wasatch National Forest, with the Salt Lake City Water Department
facts.status_note: Lookout used until about 1948; the Walker Bank Building still stands as Walker Center

access.note: Privately owned (owned and operated by Wells Fargo per Intermountain Histories); no source describes public roof access

events.note: Walker Bank Building completed as a sixteen-story building (the register and Forest Lookouts say fifteen stories)
Lookout established on the roof by the Wasatch National Forest and the Salt Lake City Water Department, with the bank's permission
July 1939 blaze at block U, north of Douglas, spotted from the lookout and halted by a Forest Service truck and CCC crew after burning under one acre
Jay M. Hamilton of Salt Lake City employed to occupy the station; schedule 9 a.m. to 9 p.m. per the Salt Lake Tribune report
James Sarvis, age fifteen, took the lookout post and returned to it several times
Used until about 1948 per the register; Intermountain Histories reports the Wasatch National Forest has no records of occupation after 1948
Added to the National Register of Historic Places in October 2006

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1941 Tribune report gives 9 a.m. to 9 p.m., which is twelve hours and matches Intermountain Histories' twelve-hour day; the register's 'late morning until dark' is a looser description of the same shift.

notes_for_editor: Height disagrees: 16 stories (Intermountain Histories, Clio) vs 15 (Former Fire Lookout Sites register, Forest Lookouts); the story reports both. Core dates 1939 start and about 1948 end agree across the register and Intermountain. Record status 'gone' fits; the building itself stands. The KDLY radio tower is dated only to 'the 1940s' by Clio, so it appears in the story but not in events. The roof's current state rests on a photo caption dated about 2015 and Clio; not checked against a newer source. Access is inferred from private ownership; no source addresses roof access. The record's 'U.S.Forest Service' agency is shared with the Salt Lake City Water Department. No source gives the date the alidade table was removed.
